(a) There are more than two million
✅ Correct Answer: (b) job - seekers who are already

Explanation: (b) job-seekers who are already ‘Are’ must be replaced with ‘have’ as we need to use present perfect tense (have + V3) to indicate actions that started in the past and continue into the present. Hence, ‘job-seekers who have already’ is the most appropriate answer.

📝 Spot the Error
I have the hundred reasons to not attend the meeting tomorrow.
✅ Correct Answer: (a) I have the hundred reasons

Explanation: (a) I have the hundred reasons The reasons given in the sentence are not specific and we use indefinite article for a non-specific noun. Article ‘a’ will be used as the word ‘hundred’ begins with a consonant sound. Hence, ‘I have a hundred reasons’ is the most appropriate answer.

You have said that, / as he took money from you many times, / he owes you / five thousand rupees all together.
(d) as he took money from you many times
✅ Correct Answer: (b) five thousand rupees all together

Explanation: (b) five thousand rupees all together ‘All together’ must be replaced with ‘altogether’, which means totally. Hence, ‘five thousand rupees altogether’ is the most appropriate answer. ‘On’ is used to indicate a specific occasion or day. ‘During’ is used to indicate a specific period of time. Similarly, ‘pandemic’ is a specific period of time. Hence, ‘during’ is the most appropriate answer.

📝 Sentence Improvement
Half of the property given to his sons by the businessman last year.
(a) Half of the property has been given
(b) Half of the property was given
(c) No substitution
(d) Half of the property is given
✅ Correct Answer: (b) Half of the property was given

Explanation: (b) Half of the property was given The given sentence is in the passive voice as the doer of the action is given after the preposition ‘by’. The phrase ‘last year’ indicates simple past tense. ‘Singular Sub. + was + V3’ is the correct grammatical structure for the passive voice of simple past tense. Hence, ‘Half of the property was given(V3)’ is the most appropriate answer.

📝 Spot the Error
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error: The train will be reached (1) / the station (2) / before sunrise (3) / tomorrow (4). Matriculation Level 29/07/2025 (Shift - 1)
(a) The train will be reached (1)
(b) the station (2)
(c) before sunrise (3)
(d) tomorrow. (4)
✅ Correct Answer: (a) The train will be reached (1)

Explanation: (a) The train will be reached (1) Future perfect tense is used to denote an action that will have been completed before a specific time in the future. ‘Will have + V3’ is the correct grammatical structure of future perfect tense. Therefore, ‘will be reached’ must be replaced with ‘will have reached’. Hence, ‘The train will have reached’ is the most appropriate answer.

I wonder what is the reason for her sudden departure.
(a) what the reason is for her sudden departure
(b) what the reason for her sudden departure is
(c) what is the reason her sudden departure
(d) the reason for her sudden departure is what
✅ Correct Answer: (a) what the reason is for her sudden departure

Explanation: (a) what the reason is for her sudden departure. The given sentence is an indirect question, and in such structures, the correct grammatical order after the 'wh-word' is "subject + verb," not "verb + subject." In the given sentence, "what the reason is for her sudden departure" correctly follows this structure: "what" (wh-word) + "the reason" (subject) + "is" (verb). Hence, "what the reason is for her sudden departure" is the most appropriate answer.
